bibliographic.title: Collinear antiferromagnetic order in spin-5/2 triangle lattice antiferromagnet Na3Fe(PO4)2

affiliations.text: School of Physics, Indian Institute of Science Education and Research Thiruvananthapuram-695551, India
Solid State Physics Division, Bhabha Atomic Research Centre, Mumbai 400 085, India
Dresden High Magnetic Field Laboratory (HLD-EMFL), Helmholtz-Zentrum Dresden-Rossendorf, 01328 Dresden, Germany

bibliographic.abstract: We set forth the structural and magnetic properties of the frustrated spin-5 / 2 triangle lattice antiferromagnet Na3Fe(PO4)2 examined via x-ray diffraction, magnetization, heat capacity, and neutron diffraction measurements on the polycrystalline sample. No structural distortion was detected from the temperature-dependant x-ray diffraction down to 12.5 K, except a systematic lattice contraction. The magnetic susceptibility at high temperatures agrees well with the high-temperature series expansion for a spin-5 / 2 isotropic triangular lattice antiferromagnet with an average exchange coupling of J/k B ≃ 1 . 8 K rather than a one-dimensional spin-5 / 2 chain model. This value of the exchange coupling is consistently reproduced by the saturation field of the pulse field magnetization data. It undergoes a magnetic long-range-order at T N ≃ 10 . 4 K. Neutron diffraction experiments elucidate a collinear antiferromagnetic ordering below T N with the propagation vector k = (1 , 0 , 0). An intermediate value of frustration ratio ( f ≃ 3 . 6) reflects moderate frustration in the compound which is corroborated by a reduced ordered magnetic moment of ∼ 1 . 52 µ B at 1.6 K, compared to its classical value (5 µ B). Magnetic isotherms exhibit a change of slope envisaging a field induced spin-flop transition at H SF ≃ 3 . 2 T. The magnetic field vs temperature phase diagram clearly unfold three distinct phase regimes, reminiscent of a frustrated magnet with in-plane (XY-type) anisotropy.

datasets.dataset_description: Temperature-dependent powder XRD measurement performed over the range 12.5 K ≤ T ≤ 300 K to check for structural phase transition or lattice distortion.
DC magnetization measured in the temperature range 1.8 K ≤ T ≤ 380 K and magnetic field range 0 ≤ H ≤ 7 T.
High-field magnetization measured in pulsed magnetic field up to 50 T at T = 1.4 K.
Heat capacity as a function of temperature and magnetic field measured on a small pellet.
NPD experiments carried out in the temperature range 1.6 K ≤ T ≤ 15 K to determine magnetic structure.
1D neutron-depolarization measurements performed to check for ferromagnetic-type correlations.
